steps.title: Level 1 — CSM-handled
steps.text: Standard account concerns (usage questions, minor dissatisfaction) handled directly by the assigned Customer Success Manager.

steps.title: Level 2 — VP Customer Success
steps.text: Escalate when: a customer explicitly threatens churn, requests a call with Nexora leadership, or an unresolved P1 incident has affected the account for more than 24 hours.

steps.title: Level 3 — Executive (CEO/CTO)
steps.text: Reserved for strategic accounts, contract-value accounts above €100,000 ARR, or reputational-risk situations (e.g., public complaint, data exposure incident).

timing_rules.statement: Escalate when: a customer explicitly threatens churn, requests a call with Nexora leadership, or an unresolved P1 incident has affected the account for more than 24 hours.

steps.title: Spec handoff
steps.text: Product Manager delivers a written spec to the squad's Engineering Manager.

steps.title: Sprint planning
steps.text: Squad breaks the spec into tickets, estimates, and commits to a two-week sprint.

steps.title: Development
steps.text: Engineers implement against a feature branch; Senior Engineers perform code review before merge.

steps.title: QA verification
steps.text: QA Engineer runs the test plan against a staging environment.

steps.title: Release
steps.text: DevOps Engineer deploys to production via the CI/CD pipeline, typically on a Wednesday release window.

steps.title: Post-release monitoring
steps.text: Squad monitors error rates for 48 hours post-release.

inputs.quote: Standardize how features move from specification to production release across all Engineering squads.

outputs.quote: Standardize how features move from specification to production release across all Engineering squads.

timing_rules.statement: Squad monitors error rates for 48 hours post-release.

steps.title: Confirmation
steps.text: A Support Engineer L3 reproduces the issue and confirms it is a genuine product defect (not user error or configuration issue).

steps.title: Defect logging
steps.text: L3 logs the defect in the Engineering defect tracker with severity, reproduction steps, and affected customer(s).

steps.title: Severity triage
steps.text: Engineering Manager for the relevant squad triages severity (P1–P4, aligned with incident priority definitions in PROC-SUP-002) within 1 business day.

steps.title: Fix scheduling
steps.text: P1/P2 defects are pulled into the current or next sprint. P3/P4 are backlog-prioritized in the normal roadmap process.

steps.title: Customer communication
steps.text: Support (not Engineering) owns all customer communication about defect status throughout.

steps.title: Resolution & verification
steps.text: Once fixed and released, the original L3 Support Engineer verifies the fix against the customer's reported scenario before closing the ticket.

inputs.quote: Define how a customer-reported issue confirmed as a product defect moves from Support into Engineering's backlog.

outputs.quote: Define how a customer-reported issue confirmed as a product defect moves from Support into Engineering's backlog.

known_gaps.heading: Known Gap — KG-02
known_gaps.text: This process does not document what happens when a customer reports a bug on a deprecated product version that is no longer receiving active development (e.g., a legacy NexFlow configuration mode retired from new sales but still running for a small number of legacy customers). In practice, these reports are currently triaged case-by-case by the Engineering Manager with no documented standard, which has led to inconsistent customer communication in at least two known cases.

timing_rules.statement: Approved expenses are reimbursed in the next payroll cycle following approval, typically within 10 business days.

steps.title: Request
steps.text: Requester submits a purchase request via the internal procurement tool, including business justification.

steps.title: Manager approval
steps.text: Direct manager approves.

steps.title: Threshold approval
steps.text: Purchases €1,000–€10,000 require Finance Manager approval; above €10,000 requires CFO approval.

steps.title: Vendor setup
steps.text: Operations Analyst confirms the vendor is set up in the finance system (new vendors require a basic due-diligence check).

steps.title: Purchase order issuance
steps.text: Finance issues a PO; vendor invoices are matched against the PO at payment time (see PROC-FIN-003).

steps.text: Contract terms (from signed SOW) are entered into the billing system at deal close, creating the formal customer account record (see glossary.md TN-004 — this is the "account" in Finance's sense, distinct from "client" in Sales' sense).
Invoices are generated per the contract's billing cadence (monthly, quarterly, or annual — most Nexora contracts are annual, paid upfront).
AP/AR Specialist monitors payment status; overdue invoices (30+ days) trigger an automatic reminder, then escalation to the account's Customer Success Manager at 45 days.
Vendor invoices are matched against the originating purchase order (PROC-FIN-002).
Approved invoices are paid on Nexora's standard 30-day payment terms unless a vendor contract specifies otherwise.

steps.title: Pre-start
steps.text: HR Generalist sends welcome pack and Day-1 logistics; IT Support Specialist provisions standard access (email, chat, HR portal — see PROC-IT-001) to be ready before Day 1.

steps.title: Day 1
steps.text: Hiring Manager and HR Generalist run orientation; new hire completes employment paperwork.

steps.title: First week
steps.text: New hire completes department-specific onboarding tasks assigned by Hiring Manager; for employees relocating to Germany, HR also shares the New Joiner Life & Settling In materials (see new_joiner_care.md).

steps.title: Security training
steps.text: New hires must complete mandatory security awareness training within the first 10 working days of their start date. (See Version History Note below regarding a discrepancy with an older document.)

steps.title: 30-day check-in
steps.text: HR Generalist holds a structured check-in with the new hire and Hiring Manager.

steps.title: 90-day review
steps.text: Hiring Manager completes a formal 90-day performance check-in.

timing_rules.statement: New hires must complete mandatory security awareness training within the first 10 working days of their start date.

An earlier version of new-hire onboarding guidance (see archived_new_hire_security_training_v1_ARCHIVED.md, Version 1.0, effective 2022-08-01) stated that security training must be completed "within 30 days" of start date.
This current document (Version 3.0, effective 2025-06-01) supersedes that guidance with the 10 working days requirement above.

version_notes.heading: VERSION HISTORY NOTE — Known Conflict
version_notes.text: An earlier version of new-hire onboarding guidance (see archived_new_hire_security_training_v1_ARCHIVED.md, Version 1.0, effective 2022-08-01) stated that security training must be completed "within 30 days" of start date. This current document (Version 3.0, effective 2025-06-01) supersedes that guidance with the 10 working days requirement above. The 2025-06-01 version is current; the 30-day figure should not be used going forward, but it may still appear in older printed materials or an employee's memory of what they were told during a hiring process before mid-2025.

timing_rules.statement: All new hires must complete the mandatory security awareness training module within 30 days of their start date.
*This requirement was superseded by PROC-HR-001 Version 3.0 (effective 2025-06-01), which shortened the requirement to 10 working days.
Germany-based employees (LOC-MUC, LOC-BER): 28 days/year, per German statutory minimum plus company standard.
India-based employees (LOC-BLR): 24 days/year plus public holidays per Karnataka state calendar.
US-based employees (LOC-AUS): 20 days/year (company policy; no federal statutory minimum applies).
UK-based employees (LOC-LON): 25 days/year plus UK public holidays.
All leave is requested and approved through the HR self-service portal; manager approval required for leave exceeding 5 consecutive working days.

steps.title: Kickoff
steps.text: Implementation Consultant reviews the AE's "Deal Closed" handoff record and schedules a kickoff call within 5 business days of contract signature.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.text: Consultant confirms configuration requirements (e.g., NexFlow batch/lot tracking, NexConnect data sources) directly with the customer.

steps.title: Configuration & data migration
steps.text: Consultant (or Solutions Architect, for custom integrations) configures the tenant and migrates initial data.

steps.title: Training
steps.text: Consultant delivers admin and end-user training sessions.

steps.title: Go-live sign-off
steps.text: The Implementation Manager provides final go-live approval after Consultant confirms all discovery items are resolved.

steps.title: Handoff to Customer Success
steps.text: Implementation Manager and the assigned Customer Success Manager hold a formal handoff call; open items are logged in the account record.

known_gaps.heading: Known Gap — KG-01
known_gaps.text: This process assumes the AE's "Deal Closed" handoff record is complete. It does not specify what the Implementation Consultant should do if the handoff record is missing required fields (e.g., agreed go-live date not documented). In practice this causes kickoff delays; there is no formal fallback procedure. ---

timing_rules.statement: All role-specific access is reviewed quarterly by IT/Security in coordination with each approving manager; unused access (no login in 90 days) is automatically revoked pending manager confirmation.

steps.title: Mandatory Security Training
steps.text: All employees must complete annual security awareness training. See PROC-HR-001 (Employee Onboarding) for the new-hire deadline — note there is a known version discrepancy between HR onboarding materials on this deadline; this document (PROC-IT-002) does not itself set the deadline, HR does.

steps.title: Customer Data Handling
steps.text: Customer production data may only be accessed by employees with an approved, logged business reason (see PROC-IT-001).

steps.title: Device Security
steps.text: Company laptops must have disk encryption and endpoint protection enabled; personal devices may not access customer production data.

steps.title: Incident Reporting
steps.text: Any suspected data exposure must be reported to the CISO within 24 hours of discovery, regardless of confirmed severity (see PROC-SUP-002).

steps.title: Data Retention
steps.text: Customer data is retained per the signed contract's data retention terms; default is 90 days post-contract-termination unless otherwise specified.

timing_rules.statement: Any suspected data exposure must be reported to the CISO within 24 hours of discovery, regardless of confirmed severity (see PROC-SUP-002).
Customer data is retained per the signed contract's data retention terms; default is 90 days post-contract-termination unless otherwise specified.

steps.title: Lead capture
steps.text: Marketing-qualified leads (MQLs) enter NexCRM automatically from web forms, webinar signups, and outbound campaigns.

steps.title: Initial scoring
steps.text: Demand Generation Manager's lead-scoring model assigns a score 0–100 based on company size, industry, and engagement behavior.

steps.title: SDR triage
steps.text: Leads scoring above 60 are assigned to an SDR within 1 business day.

steps.title: Discovery call
steps.text: SDR runs a 15-minute qualification call using the standard BANT-style discovery script (Budget, Authority, Need, Timeline).

steps.title: Qualification decision
steps.text: SDR marks the lead as Sales Qualified Lead (SQL) or Disqualified, with a reason code.

steps.title: Handoff to AE
steps.text: SQLs are assigned to an Account Executive based on territory (geography) and, for larger deals, industry specialization.

timing_rules.statement: Leads scoring above 60 are assigned to an SDR within 1 business day.
SDR must action every MQL within 1 business day of assignment.
Leads unactioned after 3 business days are automatically re-queued and flagged to the Sales Manager.

steps.title: Scoping call
steps.text: AE confirms which products, tiers, and (if applicable) custom development or complex integration needs apply. Complex integration scope requires a Solutions Architect review before quoting (see DOC-PROD-NEXCONNECT).

steps.title: Quote generation
steps.text: AE builds the quote in NexCRM using standard pricing tables.

steps.title: Discount approval
steps.text: Discounts up to 15% require no additional approval. 15–30% requires Sales Manager approval. Above 30%, or any multi-year term, requires VP Sales approval.

steps.title: Proposal delivery
steps.text: AE sends the proposal (quote + SOW) to the prospect, typically with a 30-day validity window.

steps.title: Contract signature
steps.text: Once signed, AE triggers the "Deal Closed" handoff record for Implementation (see PROC-IMPL-001, Step 1).

outputs.quote: Once signed, AE triggers the "Deal Closed" handoff record for Implementation (see PROC-IMPL-001, Step 1).

known_gaps.heading: Known Gap
known_gaps.text: This process does not currently specify what happens if a customer requests mid-negotiation changes to committed go-live dates after a proposal has already been approved at a given discount tier. In practice this is resolved ad hoc between the AE and Sales Manager; no formal escalation path exists.

steps.title: Intake
steps.text: Ticket created via customer portal, email, or (Priority tier only) phone.

steps.title: Triage (L1)
steps.text: L1 Support Engineer classifies ticket type (question, known issue, potential bug) and priority (P1–P4, see PROC-SUP-002).

steps.title: First response
steps.text: Per SLA tier (see DOC-PROD-IMPLSUP).

steps.title: Resolution or escalation
steps.text: L1 resolves known issues directly. Unresolved or complex issues escalate to L2, then L3 if a product defect is suspected.

steps.title: Bug confirmation path
steps.text: If L3 confirms a product defect, PROC-ENG-002 is triggered.

steps.title: Closure
steps.text: Ticket closed with resolution notes; customer receives a closure summary.

triggers.quote: If L3 confirms a product defect, PROC-ENG-002 is triggered.

steps.title: Detection
steps.text: Via monitoring alert (DevOps), Support ticket escalation, or direct customer report.

steps.title: Incident declaration
steps.text: Any P1 is declared a formal incident; IT Manager or on-call DevOps Engineer opens an incident channel.

steps.title: Response
steps.text: Relevant Engineering squad and DevOps investigate; Support Team Lead owns customer communication cadence (updates at least every 2 hours during an active P1).

steps.title: Resolution
steps.text: Fix deployed or mitigation applied; incident downgraded or closed.

steps.title: Post-incident review
steps.text: Required for all P1 incidents within 5 business days; owned by the Engineering Manager of the affected squad, reviewed by CISO if the incident involved any data exposure risk.
